summary:
Mission Forge is an interactive, browser-based educational game designed to introduce players to the challenges of planning and executing space exploration missions. By combining strategic decision-making, simplified engineering simulations, and NASA scientific resources, the project aims to make space mission design accessible, engaging, and educational.

Players take on the role of mission designers, selecting destinations such as the Moon, Mars, or an asteroid. They must configure spacecraft systems, allocate limited resources, balance mission costs, and evaluate engineering constraints before launching their missions.

The game is designed to demonstrate how factors such as spacecraft mass, power availability, scientific instruments, and communication capabilities influence mission feasibility and success.

Through interactive challenges, mission simulations, and performance feedback, Mission Forge encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of real-world space exploration.

Our vision is to transform complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible learning experience that inspires students, aspiring engineers, and future space explorers.
details:
Mission Forge — Project Details

Project Overview

Mission Forge is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that introduces players to the engineering, scientific, and strategic challenges involved in space exploration.

The project is designed around a central question: What does it take to transform an ambitious space exploration idea into a feasible mission?

Rather than simply controlling a spacecraft, players assume the role of mission designers responsible for making important engineering decisions throughout the mission development process.

How the Game Works

Mission Forge follows a five-stage gameplay structure:

1. Mission Selection

Players choose an exploration destination, such as the Moon, Mars, or an asteroid. Each destination presents different mission objectives and design considerations.

2. Spacecraft Configuration

Players select essential spacecraft components, including propulsion systems, power supplies, communication equipment, and scientific instruments.

Each component influences mission characteristics such as mass, energy requirements, scientific capability, and cost.

3. Resource Management

Players must design their spacecraft within predefined engineering constraints.

The game challenges players to balance limited resources while maintaining sufficient scientific and operational capabilities.

4. Mission Simulation

Once the spacecraft configuration is finalized, players initiate a simplified mission simulation.

The game evaluates design decisions and introduces mission scenarios that demonstrate the consequences of engineering trade-offs.

5. Mission Evaluation

At the end of each mission, players receive performance feedback based on mission feasibility, resource efficiency, scientific capability, and mission outcomes.

Players can use this feedback to improve their designs and attempt new missions.

Technical Implementation

Mission Forge is designed as a lightweight, browser-based application using accessible web technologies.

The proposed development stack includes:

  • HTML5: Application structure and interactive game screens.
  • CSS3: Responsive layouts, visual effects, animations, and interface design.
  • JavaScript: Gameplay logic, spacecraft configuration, resource calculations, and mission evaluation.
  • NASA scientific resources: Reference information for planetary environments and space mission design.
  • GitHub Pages: Public hosting and project accessibility.

The simulation uses simplified educational models rather than claiming to reproduce high-fidelity spacecraft engineering calculations.

Innovation and Creativity

Mission Forge combines interactive learning with engineering-based decision-making.

Its central innovation is transforming space mission planning into an accessible game in which players learn through experimentation.

Instead of memorizing aerospace concepts, players experience the consequences of design decisions and discover why engineering trade-offs matter.

The game is designed to encourage iterative problem-solving: players can analyze unsuccessful mission configurations, revise their designs, and improve their performance.

Educational Value and Intended Impact

Mission Forge aims to make space science and engineering more approachable for students and beginners.

The project encourages:

  • Scientific curiosity and interest in space exploration.
  • Systems thinking and engineering decision-making.
  • Resource optimization and strategic planning.
  • Understanding of spacecraft subsystems.
  • Experimentation, creativity, and problem-solving.

By presenting mission design as an interactive challenge, Mission Forge seeks to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.

Design Considerations

The project prioritizes accessibility, educational value, scientific transparency, and practical implementation.

Particular attention is given to creating an intuitive interface, understandable mission constraints, meaningful feedback, and gameplay that can run in a standard web browser.

The ultimate objective is to demonstrate that learning the fundamentals of space mission design can be both technically meaningful and enjoyable.
